title: Integrating Expert Knowledge in Autonomous Microscopy to Accelerate Discovery
content: Recent advancements in AI-powered automated and autonomous microscopy have dramatically transformed the exploration of material properties at the nanoscale. In our earlier work, we have developed microscopy automation platform AEcroscopy [1,2] and task specific machine learning algorithms that enable autonomous, real-time decision-making in scanning probe microscopy (SPM) [3,4], eliminating the need for human intervention in parameter tuning during experiments. However, existing autonomous experiment workflows, which are built based on experts’ prior knowledge and expectation of experiment system, often fall short in their ability to manage the vast variability in real time experiments. To overcome these limitations, we have now implemented a Gated Active Learning (GAL) framework with cost-driven acquisition [5], which allows to incorporate expert knowledge and address outlier experimental results in real time, as well as adjust excessive local exploration, to further refine and improve autonomous microscopy experiments. GAL introduces dynamic gating mechanisms in the Bayesian Optimization framework, optimizing the efficiency of the exploration by focusing on the most promising areas of the parameter space and the most informative experimental outcomes. Integrating human expertise and prior knowledge into the experimental workflow enhances the decision-making process and enables more nuanced exploration of material functionalities. The implementation of this approach in our established autonomous SPM techniques not only advances the capabilities of autonomous microscopy but also sets a precedent for applying these methods to other microscopy techniques to accelerate discovery in materials science and physics [6].
